ticket: W7-01 — GitHub paginated reconciliation (removes the 25-repo cap)
goal: Remove the hard 25-repository ceiling from the GitHub App install callback and the manual reconcile endpoint by moving repository discovery off the request path onto a paginated, resumable, tenant-scoped background job whose dispatch state lives in Postgres (a second transactional outbox alongside migration 0012's), surface the resulting in-progress state to the workspace canvas so a large installation reads as "partially imported" rather than "empty" or "complete at 25", and let an admin-triggered reconcile close the loop in the destructive direction by revoking repositories a fully-observed GitHub listing no longer reports.

acceptanceCriteria.text: handleGithubAppCallback performs no repository listing and no queue call: it verifies state, authorizes the installation, and in one withOrgContext transaction writes the installation row plus a pending github_installation_sync row (reason: 'app_install'), then kicks the discovery dispatcher after commit and returns { redirectTo, discovery: 'queued' }. No GitHub repo-list call and no BullMQ enqueue() happen on the request path.

The constants MAX_REPOS_PER_CALLBACK (25) and MAX_RECONCILE_REPOS (25), the allRepos.slice(0, …) second cap, the truncated result flag, and GithubAppClient.listInstallationRepos (with its maxRepos parameter) no longer exist anywhere in the repository.

listInstallationReposPage(installationId, page, perPage?) fetches exactly one page (GET /installation/repositories?per_page=<perPage>&page=<page>, default perPage 100) and returns { repos, page, hasNextPage, totalCount }, where hasNextPage is true iff the page came back full.
For a 120-repo fixture installation, discovery issues exactly 2 page requests (page 1 full, page 2 with 20) and yields each of the 120 repositories exactly once.

Discovery registers every discovered repository via registerRepository and enqueues exactly one repo.initial_parse outbox row per repository that has both a default branch and a HEAD sha, built by the unchanged buildInitialParseEnvelope; the 120-repo fixture ends with status = 'complete' and counts matching the fixture.
Each page's registrations, outbox rows, and cursor advance commit in a single transaction before the next page is fetched, and no network call is made while a transaction is open.
A run interrupted after page 1 resumes at page 2 on the next attempt: page 1 is not re-fetched, and no duplicate repository rows or outbox rows are produced.
For the >=100-repo fixture, every repository is registered and its parse job enqueued within INSTALLATION_DISCOVERY_TARGET_MS (60000 ms) of the install callback returning.

Discovery runs as job type github.installation_discovery on the existing github-sync queue; QUEUE_NAMES is unchanged, and the git-sync worker still routes every repo.* envelope to syncGitMetadata with identical behaviour.

reconcileInstallationRepositories performs no inline repo listing, registration or revocation: it records one durable manual_reconcile run row per active installation (carrying the ctx-derived subject), kicks the dispatcher, and returns { status: 'queued', installations, queued }; POST /integrations/github/reconcile responds 202 and remains authenticate() + authorize('admin') gated.

GET /repositories returns a sync object { status, updatedAt, discoveredRepositories, registeredRepositories, revokedRepositories, sweepOutcome } derived only from the caller's own org rows, with status resolving in the documented precedence (importing -> stalled -> failed -> idle).

sync.discoveredRepositories, sync.registeredRepositories, sync.revokedRepositories and sync.sweepOutcome are populated for an admin/owner caller and null for a member caller, while sync.status is present for both.

Tenant isolation: discovery takes org_id only from the envelope (written server-side from the leased row, never from client input), re-verifies it against resolveInstallationOrg before any write, and performs every tenant read/write inside withOrgContext; github_installation_sync has RLS enabled and forced with the standard org_isolation policy, and sayre_app holds no DELETE on it.

No credential or provider text escapes: the installation token is minted only through GithubAppClient, and neither the sync row, the queue payload, nor any log line contains a token, private key, GitHub response body, or provider error message — last_error_code is restricted to provider_unavailable | page_limit_exceeded | internal_error by both the TypeScript type and a SQL CHECK constraint.

Page bookkeeping advances by compare-and-set on the stored cursor and run id: a second runner (or a replayed job) whose expected page or run id no longer matches stops immediately as superseded, and reprocessing the same page produces no duplicate repository rows, duplicate outbox rows, or double-counted progress.

The workspace shows a partial-sync indicator while sync.status is importing or stalled — as the canvas state when no repository is selectable yet, and as a chip alongside the canvas once repositories are listed — the catalog is re-polled while a sync is in flight, and both the indicator and the polling stop once status returns to idle.

Migration 0020_w7_01_github_installation_sync.sql creates the table with the FK to organizations, the (org_id, installation_id) unique constraint, the status/reason/error-code/sweep-outcome/subject/count CHECK constraints, the org_isolation RLS policy under ENABLE + FORCE, the set_updated_at trigger, and a sayre_app grant of SELECT/INSERT plus column-scoped UPDATE and no DELETE; schema.ts and drizzle/meta/_journal.json are updated to match.

The same migration establishes the dispatch boundary: the dispatch bookkeeping columns and the partial due index; the sayre_installation_discovery_dispatcher role created NOLOGIN/NOINHERIT/NOBYPASSRLS with no memberships (failing loudly if it pre-exists with unsafe attributes); column-scoped SELECT/UPDATE and dispatcher-only policies for that role, with no INSERT/DELETE and no access to counters, cursor, or requesting subject; three SECURITY DEFINER functions owned by it with pinned search_path and range-checked parameters, EXECUTE revoked from PUBLIC and granted to sayre_app; and the additive repositories.last_discovery_run_id / last_discovery_at columns (also added to rls_acceptance.tester.test.ts's column spec).

Outbox-first dispatch: the only code that calls BullMQ enqueue() for github.installation_discovery is the dispatcher, acting on a row it holds a lease on. Both the install callback and reconcile commit their rows first and merely kick() afterwards, so dropping the kick entirely delays the job but never loses it.

Total Redis loss recovery, no human in the loop: given a running row whose cursor is at page k and whose BullMQ job has been destroyed, the dispatcher re-claims the row once next_attempt_at elapses, re-enqueues the same logical run (same run_id, same idempotency_key), and the run resumes at page k and reaches complete — with no duplicate repository rows, no duplicate repo.initial_parse outbox rows, and no admin reconcile required.

Dispatch failures are bounded and lossless: a failed enqueue() releases the lease with exponential backoff (row stays claimable, dispatch_attempt_count incremented), a process death after enqueue() but before the completion mark is recovered by lease expiry, and the resulting duplicate delivery is absorbed as superseded by the claim/CAS guards.

assertInstallationDiscoveryOutboxReady runs at startup alongside the existing gates and fails closed on a missing function, a widened ACL, an unsafe owner role, or sayre_app holding any read/write on the lease columns; index.ts starts the dispatcher, installs its wake handler, and on shutdown clears the handler, stop()s it, and closes the BullMQ queues.

Heartbeat: every committed page pushes next_attempt_at forward by INSTALLATION_DISCOVERY_REDISPATCH_SECONDS, so a run making progress is never redispatched concurrently, while a run that stops progressing becomes due again within that interval.

Destructive direction (the OQ-4 reversal of W2-09's OQ-5): when a manual_reconcile run finishes every page and reaches complete, every active GitHub repository in that org not reported by the observed listings is soft-revoked via markRepositoryRevoked in the same transaction as completion; revoked_count and sweep_outcome = 'applied' are recorded, and repository rows and graph history are retained.

Authorization: a sweep can only occur on a run whose stored reason is manual_reconcile — i.e. one created by the authenticate() + authorize('admin') endpoint. An app_install run never revokes anything even when it completes with repositories missing, no webhook path gains a revoke, and nothing about the sweep can be influenced by request input: the authorization decision is captured on the row at creation time and re-read from the row by the worker.

Audit trail: the run row records requested_by_subject_type/requested_by_subject_id (server-derived from AuthContext, null for app_install), revoked_count, sweep_outcome, completed_at and completed_run_id; each revoked repository keeps its row with revoked_at set; exactly one structured log line per sweep carries the outcome code and counts and no repository name or provider text; and an admin can read the outcome back through GET /repositories's sync.

Four independent false-positive guards, each of which revokes nothing and records its own outcome: (a) a run that fails, is cancelled, or is superseded never sweeps (not_applicable); (b) withheld_coverage when any active installation of the org has no completed run; (c) withheld_empty_result when the run discovered zero repositories while the org holds at least one active repository; (d) withheld_ratio when candidates exceed both MIN_SWEEP_RATIO_EXEMPT_ROWS and MAX_SWEEP_REVOKE_FRACTION of the org's active repositories.

Reversibility: a repository revoked by a sweep and later reported again by GitHub is re-activated (revoked_at cleared, marker restamped) by the next discovery run or installation_repositories added webhook, and is re-enqueued for parse when it has a HEAD.

Revoke call sites remain structurally enumerable: after this ticket exactly two code paths can move repositories.revoked_at — applyRemoved (the removed webhook) and the discovery sweep — and neither ReconcileDeps nor any other request-path service declares or reaches a markRepositoryRevoked dependency. W2-09's trace-through test is replaced by an equally structural test asserting exactly this, not deleted.

edgeCases.text: Installation with zero accessible repositories: page 1 returns empty, hasNextPage false, sync ends complete with all counts 0, and no outbox row is written.

Installation with exactly 100 repositories (page-size boundary): page 1 is full so page 2 is fetched, returns empty, and the run completes with exactly 100 registered — no repo registered twice, none missed.
A repository with no default branch or no HEAD sha (empty repo): registered but not enqueued; it increments registered_count and not enqueued_count, matching today's callback behaviour.

GitHub returns 5xx / a network error on page 3 of 5: pages 1–2 stay committed, the row is marked failed with provider_unavailable and the cursor still at 3, the handler rethrows so BullMQ retries with backoff, and a later attempt resumes at page 3.
Installation suspended or uninstalled mid-discovery: the next loop iteration's active check fails, the row is marked cancelled, and no further repository or outbox row is written.
Envelope names an installation id that no longer resolves, or resolves to a different org than envelope.org_id: the run performs zero writes and ends cancelled (unknown_installation / org_mismatch).
Callback with setup_action=request (GitHub sends no installation_id): no sync row, no dispatcher kick, result { discovery: 'skipped' }.
Callback for an installation already bound to a different org: still throws InstallationOrgConflictError before any sync row is written or any dispatch occurs.

The dispatcher's BullMQ enqueue() fails (Redis unreachable) after the pending row committed: the callback has already redirected successfully, the lease is released with bounded backoff, dispatch_attempt_count increments, the row stays pending and claimable, and the work is dispatched automatically once Redis returns — no manual reconcile is required (revision 2, OQ-3). Until then the catalog reports importing, then stalled past INSTALLATION_SYNC_STALL_MS.
Duplicate/redelivered discovery job after a run already completed: claimInstallationSync returns null (status complete), the run exits without re-fetching or re-writing anything.

GitHub reorders repositories between pages so one repo appears on two pages: the registerRepository upsert and the outbox's (org_id, idempotency_key) DO NOTHING make the second occurrence a no-op — no duplicate rows, and no duplicate repo.initial_parse delivery.

Malformed page response (missing/non-array repositories, malformed full_name, blank default branch, non-hex HEAD sha, oversized body, bad Content-Length): normalized to GithubAppApiError, the page is not committed, the cursor does not move, and the run fails with provider_unavailable.
total_count absent, negative, non-integer, or absurdly large: stored as null; progress reports registered counts only and never fabricates a denominator.

An installation that keeps reporting full pages past MAX_INSTALLATION_DISCOVERY_PAGES (100 pages ~ 10000 repositories): the loop stops at the ceiling, marks the row failed with page_limit_exceeded, and does not rethrow (a retry cannot help); the dispatcher's due predicate excludes that error code, so it is not redispatched either.
Invalid arguments to listInstallationReposPage (page < 1, non-integer, perPage 0, negative, > 100, non-integer): GithubAppApiError is thrown before any network call and before any token mint.

Member (non-admin) caller of GET /repositories: sync.status and sync.updatedAt are present, every admin-gated field is null, and the payload leaks no installation id, account login, or name of a repository the member cannot read.

Unauthenticated or member caller of POST /integrations/github/reconcile: 401 / 403 respectively (unchanged), and no sync row is written, no dispatcher kick occurs, and — because no manual_reconcile row exists — no sweep can subsequently run on their behalf.

Two organizations syncing simultaneously: each org's /repositories sync reflects only its own rows, enforced by RLS plus the explicit org predicate; neither org's counts move because of the other's discovery.

Re-running discovery for an org whose repositories are already registered (including ones previously revoked): repositories are upserted with revoked_at cleared, no duplicate rows appear, and counts reflect repositories processed in this run.

A running row abandoned by a dead worker and older than INSTALLATION_SYNC_STALL_MS: a new startInstallationSync resets it to a fresh pending run with a new run_id, while a running row touched within the window is left alone ({ reset: false }) so a live run is never restarted underneath itself.

Web deploy skew: a /repositories payload with no sync key parses as { status: 'idle' }; a payload with a present but malformed sync (unknown status string, non-numeric counts, unparseable updatedAt) throws RepositoryCatalogResponseError rather than silently rendering an importing state; unknown extra keys inside sync are ignored.

UI termination: once sync.status returns to idle and no repository is still registered, the 2.5s catalog re-poll stops and the indicator unmounts — no unbounded polling loop, and no indicator left stuck on screen after a completed import.

Redis entirely unavailable for the whole dispatch window: rows accumulate as pending, every claim/publish cycle defers with backoff, nothing is lost or double-counted, and when Redis returns every accumulated row dispatches and completes.

Redis flushed mid-run (row running, cursor at page 3 of 5, job object gone): the heartbeat stops advancing, next_attempt_at elapses, the dispatcher redispatches the same run_id, and the run resumes at page 3 and completes — pages 1–2 are not re-fetched and counters are not double-counted.

Two core replicas dispatching concurrently: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED plus the lease means each due row is claimed by exactly one dispatcher; if a duplicate job still reaches a worker, claimInstallationSync/advanceInstallationSyncPage's CAS ends it as superseded.

Dispatcher dies after enqueue() succeeded but before the completion mark: the lease expires, the row is redispatched, and the second job either resumes safely or exits superseded; at-least-once dispatch never produces a duplicate repository or outbox row.

A permanently undispatchable row (e.g. an installation whose every attempt fails): dispatch_attempt_count reaches MAX_INSTALLATION_DISCOVERY_DISPATCH_ATTEMPTS (10) and the row stops being due — no infinite redispatch loop — while the catalog keeps reporting stalled / failed to admins.
Terminal rows are never claimed: complete, cancelled, and failed with page_limit_exceeded all fall outside the dispatcher's due predicate.

The cross-tenant claim cannot leak: each claimed row yields only its own org_id into the envelope, the dispatcher never opens an org context and never touches a tenant table, and privilege-level assertions confirm sayre_app can neither read nor write the lease/dispatch columns while the dispatcher role can neither INSERT/DELETE nor read counters, cursor, or the requesting subject.

Transient GitHub failure misread as "repo no longer present" (the primary false-positive risk of OQ-4): a manual_reconcile run gets a 502 on page 4 of 5. The run fails with the cursor at 4, sweep_outcome stays not_applicable, and zero repositories are revoked; only the later attempt that fetches every page and reaches complete may sweep, and it then revokes exactly the genuinely-absent repositories.

GitHub returns HTTP 200 with an empty repository list (installation permissions narrowed, or token scoped down) while the org holds 40 active repositories: the run completes but the sweep records withheld_empty_result and revokes nothing.

GitHub reports only 3 of 100 repositories across a fully-paginated, error-free run (a partial provider outage returning 200s): 97 candidates exceed both the row floor and the 50% fraction, so the sweep records withheld_ratio and revokes nothing; an admin sees the withheld outcome in GET /repositories's sync.

Multi-installation org: installation A's reconcile run completes while installation B has never completed a run. The sweep records withheld_coverage and revokes nothing, so B's repositories can never be revoked by A's run. Once both have completed runs, only repositories absent from both observed listings are revoked.

A repository added by the installation_repositories added webhook mid-run, after its page was already fetched: its updated_at is later than the run's started_at, so the candidate query excludes it and it is not revoked despite carrying no marker for this run.

An app_install run that completes while several held repositories are absent from GitHub's listing: nothing is revoked, sweep_outcome is not_applicable, and the run is otherwise a normal successful discovery.

A candidate that is already revoked: the candidate query only selects revoked_at IS NULL rows, and markRepositoryRevoked's COALESCE keeps an existing timestamp fixed, so revoked_count never counts a re-revoke and no timestamp advances on a repeated sweep.

A sweep-revoked repository re-granted on GitHub: the next discovery run registers it again with revoked_at cleared and the current run marker, and re-enqueues repo.initial_parse when it has a default branch and HEAD.

Revocation is unreachable from any non-admin surface: no member/unauthenticated request, no webhook payload field, and no queue payload field can cause or target a sweep — the only inputs are the row's own reason/run_id and the server's own paginated observation — and a member's GET /repositories shows revokedRepositories/sweepOutcome as null.
